1.explanation: This minimal example uses a narrow Menu and Select to force text overflow and demonstrate that by default Next’s Menu.Item and Select.Option attach a title attribute for screen‐reader and hover support.  Hovering over the long pure‐string entry and the Icon+text entry in the Menu, as well as the long Select option, will all produce tooltips.  You can use this code as a starting point to test changes such as only adding title when children is a pure string or providing a ConfigProvider API to toggle title rendering.
1.bug_scenario:
When Menu.Item (and similar dropdown components such as Select) auto‐attach a title attribute on every item, two problems arise:
1.  If the children of Menu.Item is a complex node (Icon plus text) the user will still see a folded tooltip for overflow text even when they don’t want it.
2.  If the innerText and the title are identical (pure‐string children), it violates WCAG’s “no redundant text” guidance and produces an unwanted hover popup.

In the screenshots you can see:
- A long pure‐string Menu.Item showing its title on hover
- A Menu.Item with an Icon + text still showing a tooltip
- A Select.Option with a long label showing a tooltip, even when the user doesn’t want a hover bubble
